ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.title: 福尔摩斯从哪来
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.body: 歇洛克·福尔摩斯首次出现在 1887 年《比顿圣诞年刊》的中篇《血字的研究》。作者阿瑟·柯南·道尔当时还是个不太成功的医生，写侦探小说原是贴补诊所的收入。这个苏格兰医生后来靠福尔摩斯封爵、又恨福尔摩斯占掉自己的历史小说时间——爱恨都写在这篇前言里。

ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.title: 作者想杀掉自己的主角
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.body: 1891 年道尔写信给母亲：考虑把福尔摩斯干掉，一了百了。两年后《最后一案》真让他和莫里亚蒂一起跌进莱辛巴赫瀑布。读者抗议太猛，1903 年《空屋》又把人救回来。侦探小说很少有这么公开的作者—角色战争。

ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.title: 真正的老师是爱伦·坡
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.body: 这篇前言把谱系说得很清楚：神探配一个相对笨拙的同伴、用报纸启事把人召到侦探住所，都来自爱伦·坡 1841 年的《莫格街凶杀案》（ Dupin / 译文里的「杜邦」）。书架上现在有这本公版原作，打开就能对上福尔摩斯的配方。

ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.title: 《波希米亚丑闻》对《失窃的信》
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.body: 前言还点了另一篇坡：最显眼的东西藏在最显眼的地方。《波希米亚丑闻》里福尔摩斯去偷回一封要命的信，直接对应坡的《失窃的信》。两套探案是师生关系，不是平行宇宙。

ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.title: 演绎法其实是回溯推理
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.body: 福尔摩斯口中的「演绎法」，哲学上更接近皮尔士说的溯因推理（abduction）：从结果倒推最可能的原因。前言把《血字的研究》评为「提出演绎法、并贬低以前的侦探小说」——他瞧不上的，正是只靠巧合破获的老派故事。
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.anchorText: 提出演绎法的推理方法

ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.title: 苏格兰场是陪衬
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.body: 雷斯垂德、葛莱森这些苏格兰场侦探在书里的功能几乎固定：先错一次，再被福尔摩斯纠正。维多利亚时代伦敦警察厅（Scotland Yard）刚建立刑事侦查处不久，私家侦探作为「公职侦探力所难及」的补充，是当时读者很爱看的对照。
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.anchorText: 苏格兰场的干探们显得愚笨无能

ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.title: 百分之七的溶液
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.body: 《四签名》开篇华生质问注射的是吗啡还是可卡因，福尔摩斯答「可卡因，百分之七的溶液」。1880 年代可卡因在欧美还被当作补品和局麻药卖，弗洛伊德早期甚至写过赞扬文章。译本加注提醒成瘾性——这是后来才压倒性的医学共识。
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.anchorText: 这是可卡因，百分之七的溶液

ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.title: 贝克街并不凉快
ed91998e-cb87-4934-903c-737d5ca91fc5.body: 「贝克街象一座火炉」是《硬纸盒子》的八月开场。221B Baker Street 在现实伦敦是虚构门牌（当时贝克街门号到不了 221），但现在的福尔摩斯博物馆就开在 221B，把小说地址做成了地标。

7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.title: 福尔摩斯的配方从这里来
7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.body: 开篇就点明：这本书是《福尔摩斯探案全集》前言里点名的老师。神探杜邦、略显迟钝的同伴叙事者、把相关人召到侦探住所的报纸启事——柯南·道尔几乎原样搬进了贝克街。两本对照着读，师承一眼能看出来。
7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.anchorText: 书架上那本福尔摩斯，和这本书是一对

7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.title: 杜邦：第一个现代侦探
7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.body: C. Auguste Dupin 比福尔摩斯早了四十多年。他不是警察，不住办公室，靠租来的破宅和推理过活。爱伦·坡一共只写了三篇杜邦（莫格街、玛丽·罗杰、失窃的信），却把「私家侦探 + 同伴叙事」的模型一次定型。
7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.anchorText: C. Auguste Dupin is the prototype of the modern detective

7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.title: 分析力被写成一种快感
7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.body: 故事开头不写尸体，先写「分析者」从解谜里得到的享受——像力士炫耀肌肉。福尔摩斯后来的小提琴、可卡因、不肯看普通新闻，都是这个「把推理当竞技」的性格放大版。
7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.anchorText: so glories the analyst in that moral activity which disentangles

7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.title: 密室里的非人凶手
7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.body: 莫格街的门锁从里面锁死，警方只会朝「哪个人进得去」想。杜邦的转折是：凶手不必是人。逃掉的 Borneo orangutan 用剃刀制造了那场大屠杀——密室推理的第一次经典解法，不是更聪明的人，而是分类问错了。
7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.anchorText: a very large, tawny Ourang-Outang of the Bornese species

7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.title: 那则启事，福尔摩斯用过很多次
7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.body: 杜邦不审犯人，他登广告：一只走失的猩猩，物归原主请来 Faubourg St. Germain。水手自己上门，案子就破了。福尔摩斯前言里说「如法炮制过多遍」——《血字的研究》里那种把人召到贝克街的手法，源头就是这段。
7e8c2a14-6b5f-4d91-a3e0-1c9f4b8d2e70.anchorText: The advertisement, as Dupin had anticipated, brought the sailor to our door

d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.title: Agrippa and the forbidden curriculum
d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.body: Cornelius Agrippa was a Renaissance magus; his books mix Neoplatonism with what the eighteenth century already called exploded science. Victor’s father waves him off as “sad trash,” and that shrug matters: Frankenstein’s catastrophe starts as a teenage reading list nobody bothered to correct.
d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.anchorText: a volume of the works of Cornelius Agrippa

d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.title: Galvanism: the science under the myth
d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.body: Mary Shelley was writing in the wake of Luigi Galvani and Giovanni Aldini, who made dead limbs twitch with electricity. The innkeeper’s lecture on “electricity and galvanism” is the novel’s hinge: alchemy is dumped, and a modern, laboratory kind of horror takes its place.

d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.title: A dreary night of November
d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.body: The creature is not born in a lightning-struck tower. Shelley puts the awakening on a wet November night in an attic, with a dying candle. The 1931 film invented the rooftop storm; the book’s terror is quieter and closer to a dissection room.
d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.anchorText: It was on a dreary night of November

d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.title: The creature’s three books
d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.body: In the woods the creature finds a dropped portmanteau: Paradise Lost, Plutarch’s Lives, and Goethe’s The Sorrows of Werter (Shelley’s spelling). Milton teaches him to see himself as both Adam and Satan; Plutarch offers republican virtue; Werther models passionate self-destruction. His education is a miniature Western canon.
d726a766-f064-4aca-80ea-66d5df953ab6.anchorText: Paradise Lost, a volume of Plutarch's Lives, and the Sorrows of Werter

efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.title: The green light
efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.body: Across the bay from West Egg, the light on Daisy’s dock is the novel’s emblem of wanting: close enough to see, never close enough to reach. Fitzgerald later said he almost cut it; it survived because the whole book is that stretch of the arm.
efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.anchorText: a single green light, minute and far away

efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.title: Tom’s “scientific” book is a smear
efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.body: ‘The Rise of the Coloured Empires’ by ‘this man Goddard’ is Fitzgerald’s parody of Lothrop Stoddard’s The Rising Tide of Color (1920), a real bestseller of scientific racism. Tom is not being profound; he is reciting the decade’s most respectable bigotry.
efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.anchorText: The Rise of the Coloured Empires

efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.title: The valley of ashes
efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.body: Between the Eggs and Manhattan sits a landfill of industrial waste—Fitzgerald’s image of what the party is built on. T. S. Eliot’s The Waste Land (1922) is in the air; so is the actual Flushing ash dump that later became Flushing Meadows.
efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.anchorText: This is a valley of ashes

efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.title: Doctor T. J. Eckleburg
efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.body: The faded oculist’s billboard—blue eyes, yellow spectacles, no face—hangs over the ash heap like a cheap god. George Wilson later takes the eyes for the eyes of God. The novel never confirms him; it just lets advertisement and judgment occupy the same sign.
efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.anchorText: the eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg

efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.title: Boats against the current
efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.body: The last sentence is the book in miniature: American striving as a rowing machine that only ever returns you to what you already lost. Gatsby’s future was always a refurbished past with Daisy in it.
efcf4f31-c7f0-470c-97c3-71f7ddd4ad9f.anchorText: boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past

ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.title: Evacuees, not just adventure
ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.body: The four Pevensies are sent to the Professor’s house because of the air-raids: this is the Blitz, 1940. Lewis starts in wartime England so that Narnia’s winter feels like another occupation, not a random fairy-tale climate.
ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.anchorText: sent away from London during the war because of the air–raids

ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.title: Daughter of Eve
ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.body: Mr. Tumnus’s greeting is Genesis in a faun’s mouth: Lucy is not just a girl, she is a child of Eve. Lewis, a Christian apologist, lets Narnia recognize humans the way the King James Bible names them. The Bible on this shelf is the same language.
ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.anchorText: you are a Daughter of Eve

ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.title: Always winter and never Christmas
ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.body: The White Witch’s slogan is the book’s moral weather report: time is stuck, feast days don’t come, and even the calendar has been occupied. Christmas later arriving with Father Christmas is not a cameo—it is the first crack in her magic.

ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.title: Turkish Delight as bait
ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.body: Edmund’s addiction is historically specific: lokum was a scarce wartime luxury in Britain. Lewis needed a sweet that would feel both magical and slightly sinful to a 1940s child—sugar was rationed.

ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.title: Aslan is on the move
ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.body: The name Aslan is Turkish for lion. When the Beavers whisper that he is coming, spring starts before anyone sees him. Lewis later said he did not begin by encoding the Gospels; the lion arrived, and the Passion story followed.
ca8e7c9d-d23e-43fa-85bd-1b3b71e5fae1.anchorText: They say Aslan is on the move

8d5c7530-7e88-44d4-b4c3-0c14b97fb2c2.title: The King James cadence
8d5c7530-7e88-44d4-b4c3-0c14b97fb2c2.body: Commissioned by James I in 1604 and published in 1611, this translation was meant to unify English worship. Its parallelism and thee/thou rhythm became the default sound of “Bible English,” which later writers—including Lewis in Narnia—could quote by texture alone.
8d5c7530-7e88-44d4-b4c3-0c14b97fb2c2.anchorText: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth

8d5c7530-7e88-44d4-b4c3-0c14b97fb2c2.title: Why Narnia says Daughter of Eve
8d5c7530-7e88-44d4-b4c3-0c14b97fb2c2.body: Genesis 3:20: Adam names his wife Eve, “mother of all living.” That is the line Mr. Tumnus is standing on when he calls Lucy a Daughter of Eve. Open The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe beside this page and the greeting stops being decorative.
8d5c7530-7e88-44d4-b4c3-0c14b97fb2c2.anchorText: Adam called his wife's name Eve; because she was the mother of all living

bc250ad0-8d55-4e5c-b316-697339f54062.title: The most famous first sentence in the novel
bc250ad0-8d55-4e5c-b316-697339f54062.body: Austen’s opening is a joke dressed as a proverb: society agrees that a rich bachelor must want a wife—because the neighborhood wants him for its daughters. The irony is the whole marriage market in one clause.
bc250ad0-8d55-4e5c-b316-697339f54062.anchorText: It is a truth universally acknowledged

bc250ad0-8d55-4e5c-b316-697339f54062.title: Netherfield is the matchmakers’ weather
bc250ad0-8d55-4e5c-b316-697339f54062.body: A rented estate next door is not scenery; it is a plot device. Mrs. Bennet hears that Netherfield Park is let and immediately starts deploying daughters. In a novel without duels, real estate is the opening gun.
bc250ad0-8d55-4e5c-b316-697339f54062.anchorText: Netherfield Park is let at last

bc250ad0-8d55-4e5c-b316-697339f54062.title: Darcy enters as a snub
bc250ad0-8d55-4e5c-b316-697339f54062.body: The room first admires Darcy’s “fine, tall person,” then drops him when he won’t dance. Pride in this book is social temperature: attractive until it refuses to perform friendliness.
bc250ad0-8d55-4e5c-b316-697339f54062.anchorText: his friend Mr. Darcy soon drew the attention of the room

6f890b3b-d444-4677-8bb7-c51227fe2736.title: A misanthropist’s heaven
6f890b3b-d444-4677-8bb7-c51227fe2736.body: Lockwood’s opening joke—that he and Heathcliff are a “suitable pair to divide the desolation”—is the reader’s first trap. The tenant thinks he has found a fellow recluse; he has walked into a haunted household.
6f890b3b-d444-4677-8bb7-c51227fe2736.anchorText: Mr. Heathcliff and I are such a suitable pair to divide the desolation

6f890b3b-d444-4677-8bb7-c51227fe2736.title: I am Heathcliff
6f890b3b-d444-4677-8bb7-c51227fe2736.body: Cathy’s speech to Nelly is the novel’s theology of love: not “I love him” but identity. Victorian readers found it appalling; it still reads like a refusal of the marriage-plot’s usual arithmetic.

6f890b3b-d444-4677-8bb7-c51227fe2736.title: Two houses, one weather system
6f890b3b-d444-4677-8bb7-c51227fe2736.body: Wuthering Heights (the farm) and Thrushcross Grange (the genteel hall) are not just addresses. Brontë splits the book between raw moor and carpeted drawing-room; every character is damaged by crossing the gap.

d43868d0-b96f-43bf-83a3-faf13a286cb3.title: 开卷那首《临江仙》不是罗贯中写的
d43868d0-b96f-43bf-83a3-faf13a286cb3.body: 「滚滚长江东逝水」是明人杨慎的词，清初毛宗岗父子改定《三国演义》时拿来当卷首。电视剧《三国演义》把它做成片头曲以后，很多人以为这就是罗贯中原文——版本史上不是。

d43868d0-b96f-43bf-83a3-faf13a286cb3.title: 分久必合，合久必分
d43868d0-b96f-43bf-83a3-faf13a286cb3.body: 这八个字是全书的历史哲学：把东汉末年的乱局放进一个循环里，而不是一则道德寓言。它也给后面的桃园、赤壁、出师一个框架——人在 palindrome 里做事，不是在直线上做事。

d43868d0-b96f-43bf-83a3-faf13a286cb3.title: 桃园誓词
d43868d0-b96f-43bf-83a3-faf13a286cb3.body: 「不求同年同月同日生，只愿同年同月同日死」把异姓结拜写成一种准血缘。后文吕布破徐州、关羽降曹、刘备摔阿斗，全是在还这笔誓。它不是开场彩，是结构。
d43868d0-b96f-43bf-83a3-faf13a286cb3.anchorText: 不求同年同月同日生，只愿同年同月同日死

d43868d0-b96f-43bf-83a3-faf13a286cb3.title: 衣服与手足
d43868d0-b96f-43bf-83a3-faf13a286cb3.body: 刘备后来说「兄弟如手足，妻子如衣服」——这句被现代读者骂得最多，却是桃园逻辑的延长：政治同盟被写成身体，家庭被写成可替换的装备。毛本把伦理说得这样刺耳，是有意的。
d43868d0-b96f-43bf-83a3-faf13a286cb3.anchorText: 吾三人桃园结义，不求同生，但愿同死

aa98e6de-64d4-4e56-97de-f18791ce0f64.title: 这个版本先讲阿里巴巴
aa98e6de-64d4-4e56-97de-f18791ce0f64.body: 许多中译本把山鲁佐德的框架放在最前；这个电子本却从阿里巴巴砍柴遇盗开始。故事仍是同一组民间传奇，只是目录被重新排过——所以开卷不是「讲故事的女人」，而是「喊开门的樵夫」。

aa98e6de-64d4-4e56-97de-f18791ce0f64.title: 芝麻芝麻，把门儿开开
aa98e6de-64d4-4e56-97de-f18791ce0f64.body: 口令是谷物名，不是魔法专有名词。阿里巴巴后来急得改喊麦子、辣椒、豆子，石门不动——民间故事用「记错咒语」把贪婪写成喜剧。英语里的 Open sesame 就是这一句的通行译法。

aa98e6de-64d4-4e56-97de-f18791ce0f64.title: 山鲁佐德在书的另一头
aa98e6de-64d4-4e56-97de-f18791ce0f64.body: 框架故事仍在：暴君山鲁亚尔日娶日杀，宰相的女儿山鲁佐德用「明天再讲」活了一千零一夜。这个本子把序放在后面，但不讲她，整本书的悬念结构就少了一半。
aa98e6de-64d4-4e56-97de-f18791ce0f64.anchorText: 山鲁佐德是大女儿的芳名

2d835a36-7d9a-44e0-9895-8a03b5aeaadb.title: A novel about the idea of knighthood
2d835a36-7d9a-44e0-9895-8a03b5aeaadb.body: This Chivalry is Rafael Sabatini’s 1931 historical novel (opening: “The Lady of Rovieto”), not a treatise. Colombo da Siena is invented as the orphan of a hanged traitor, then sent into a world that already thinks chivalry is a chimera.
2d835a36-7d9a-44e0-9895-8a03b5aeaadb.anchorText: WHEN his father was hanged, his mother died of a broken heart

2d835a36-7d9a-44e0-9895-8a03b5aeaadb.title: Chivalry as an untimely ideal
2d835a36-7d9a-44e0-9895-8a03b5aeaadb.body: The narrator says Colombo is guided by ideals “belonging to the age of chivalry rather than to his own age.” The book’s tension is anachronism: knight-errantry performed after the culture has priced it as a joke.
2d835a36-7d9a-44e0-9895-8a03b5aeaadb.anchorText: lofty ideals belonging to the age of chivalry

dd57cb5b-5485-4118-8b33-b5df7c31da59.title: 兵经从哪来
dd57cb5b-5485-4118-8b33-b5df7c31da59.body: 《孙子兵法》大约成书于春秋末期，托名孙武。它被后来的兵家尊为「兵经」「百世谈兵之祖」——不是因为字数多（十三篇很短），而是因为它把战争写成可以计算的决策，而不是天命或勇气的比赛。
dd57cb5b-5485-4118-8b33-b5df7c31da59.anchorText: 被人们尊奉为“兵经”“百世谈兵之祖”

dd57cb5b-5485-4118-8b33-b5df7c31da59.title: 第一个系统作注的是曹操
dd57cb5b-5485-4118-8b33-b5df7c31da59.body: 前言写得很清楚：历史上第一个系统给《孙子兵法》作注的，是三国的曹操。书架上的《三国演义》里那个「治世能臣、乱世奸雄」，在真实历史上首先是个读兵书的人。两本可以对着看：演义给脸谱，兵法给方法。
dd57cb5b-5485-4118-8b33-b5df7c31da59.anchorText: 第一个系统为《孙子兵法》作注解的人就是三国时著名的政治家、军事家曹操

dd57cb5b-5485-4118-8b33-b5df7c31da59.title: 兵者，诡道也
dd57cb5b-5485-4118-8b33-b5df7c31da59.body: 「诡」在这里主要不是教人阴招，而是说战争的信息是不对称的：能让对手误判，才谈得上「计」。后文的示强示弱、声东击西，都是这一句的展开。把它读成厚黑学，会丢掉孙子真正在算的东西——利害与情报。

dd57cb5b-5485-4118-8b33-b5df7c31da59.title: 知彼知己
dd57cb5b-5485-4118-8b33-b5df7c31da59.body: 「知彼知己，百战不殆」出自谋攻篇，常常被缩成励志口号。原文的下一句更狠：不知彼而知己，一胜一负；两边都不知道，每战必殆。孙子把情报写成胜负比，而不是性格修养。
